about: The rpc and log --json fields a client may rely on (ADR 0048 section 6, ADR 0025 sections 4 and 5). Fields not listed here are unversioned. trellis is held to every entry by tests/modes.rs (the rpc stream, the command answers and log --json), tests/cli.rs (overview, the Atlas's answers, get_queue and get_state's fields) and tests/colibri_doctor.rs and src/hosted.rs (get_state's tier_label). Both clients are held to rpc.events and rpc.framing by tests that read every field listed there: desktop/src/state.rs every_field_in_the_rpc_contract_is_read and tui/internal/frames/frames_test.go TestFramesReadEveryContractField; and the desktop to log_json's always and optional by desktop/src/trails.rs every_trail_field_in_the_log_contract_is_read. A field that not every client reads yet is under not_every_client instead (rpc.not_every_client for events and framing, log_json.not_every_client for trail paths), in the same shape, with read_by naming the clients that read it today; those tests do not read it, nor rpc.responses. An event's fields are under its "fields" object, beside "message": those always present, those present only in the case a list is named for (a turn that called the model, a blast_radius turn, a prompt-sending driver, a response header the endpoint sent), and, under "absent_when", when a listed field is still left off. A figure trellis did not measure is absent, never 0. A <field>_values list names every value the field takes; both clients' tests send its last value and look for it in what their parser kept, so the last is one that nothing else in the record contains. A command's answer data is under "responses", per command: the fields always in it, and those present only for one value of another, as dotted paths, with [] meaning each element of an array (#559; the Atlas, owner request of 2026-10-11). framing.response's no_data names the commands that answer with no data. A response's id is the id its command was sent with, and a run's run_start and run_end carry the id of the prompt that started it.

absent_when.model_ms: the governance audit's turn event, which makes no model call (trellis-loop agent.rs ~909-919)
absent_when.prompt_bytes: the governance audit's turn event, which sends no prompt
absent_when.completion_tokens: the governance audit's turn event, which reads no reply; or a reply the step read reported no output tokens (the provider stub's replies all report them)
absent_when.queue_wait_ms: a reply the step read carried no x-colibri-queue-wait-ms header

turn.check_kind: "" on a turn that ran no check; otherwise the kind of check behind the turn's verdict, as trellis-checks names it (CheckKind, crates/trellis-checks/src/verdict.rs); the governance audit's turn is Governance
turn.about: tool, target and wrote are the trail's record of the turn, from the function the trail's action uses (#800): tool is the tool's name, target what it was pointed at, and wrote is true only for an edit that applied or a file write_file created, so a bash or custom tool's changes are not counted in it. A client takes what a turn touched from these, never from call or observation (#834, #856). elapsed_ms is the run's wall-clock spend after the turn as its budget measures it (#799): milliseconds by the monotonic clock since the loop started, with every wait on a person in approve mode and every pause (the paused and resumed events) taken out, the figure checked against run budget's max_wall_clock_ms.

absent_when.prompt_bytes: always: the driver builds the prompt inside next_step, so before the call its size is not yet measured (#614)

model call.about: sent before each model call, with the turn number the turn event it produces will carry; the governance audit's turn, which makes no call, has none. elapsed_ms is the budget's wall-clock spend as the loop checked it just before this call, measured as the turn's elapsed_ms is

run budget.about: the ceilings the run enforces, sent once as the run's loop starts and again, with every ceiling and in the same shape, at the budget check where a client's set_budget raise takes effect (ADR 0058 section 2, #807), before that iteration's model call; the latest is the one in force

absent_when.kv_slots: colibri's GET /health failed, was not colibri's shape, did not answer within the read timeout, or answered without kv_slots (a liveness-only answer)
absent_when.tiers_vram: as kv_slots, or /health answered without tiers

runtime identified.about: sent once per run, before the run's first model request, for an endpoint identified as colibri (ADR 0047 decision 13; #627); never for any other endpoint. runtime is always "colibri"; served is the model id colibri listed, cut to 200 characters. kv_slots, tiers_vram, tiers_ram and tiers_disk are colibri's own counts and are absent, never 0, when it did not report them; the three tier counts are separate figures, and no total or share is derived from them. Not in the trail (ADR 0047 decision 13).

optional.restored: when the outcome is not_converged or interrupted
optional.elapsed_ms: when the agent loop ran and returned: its wall-clock spend in milliseconds as the budget measured it, with every wait on a person in approve mode and every pause taken out, the figure the turn's elapsed_ms counts up to. Absent, never a partial figure, for a run the loop did not finish: an interrupt or abort, an error before the loop started, and a partitioned run, whose partitions each spend their own wall clock

optional.data: when success is true and the command is not one no_data names

no_data.prompt: accepted: the run's run_start and run_end follow
no_data.follow_up: accepted at once, while the run it was sent during goes on; its own run's run_start and run_end carry its id
no_data.quit: answered once any run in flight has rolled back and every other answer is written; trellis then exits

not_every_client.about: What trellis emits and a client may rely on, which not every client reads yet: listed so a rename fails trellis's tests, and kept out of rpc.events and rpc.framing, every field of which both clients' tests require their parser to keep. A record here has the keys a record there has, for the fields it adds; read_by names, per field, the clients that read it today (desktop, tui), and [] is neither yet. A field moves to rpc.events or rpc.framing once both clients read it.

event_line.about: the key of every event's line beside fields, as tracing's JSON layer writes it. The stdout layer passes trellis's events at info and above whatever RUST_LOG says (main.rs), so level is one of level_values. The TUI shows a WARN or ERROR event it has no record for as a warning.

absent_when.lines_added: any turn but an edit that applied: a refused edit, write_file, bash, a custom tool, and the governance audit's turn

turn.about: lines_added and lines_removed are the whole lines an applied edit added and removed, in every control mode, computed from the text the edit read and wrote, the same hunk an approve-mode question counts (#802); start_line is the 1-based line, in the file before the edit, of the first line it removed or replaced, or with nothing removed the line the added lines went before; diff is a unified diff of that one hunk (--- and +++ naming the path, one @@ -a,b +c,d @@ header, a line of context either side), cut at a line once it passes 8192 bytes with a last line saying how many diff lines were cut, while the counts stay the whole edit's. diff is repository text and model output: a client shows it as text and never interprets it (CLAUDE.md rule 10). duration_ms is the tool call's time in milliseconds by the monotonic clock, with any wait on a person in approve mode taken out, and on the governance audit's turn the audit's own time (#800); summarised is how many of the radius's call sites its observation summarised by file instead of listing them, 0 when it listed every one. completion_tokens_used is the counter run budget's max_tokens is checked against: completion (output) tokens over every reply so far, format retries included, never prompt tokens and never a sum of the two; a hosted driver counts a reply that reported none at its request's max_tokens, so the ceiling trips early rather than never; 0 for a driver that reads no reply (the scripted one).

absent_when.context_bytes: the driver elides nothing and has no ceiling: the scripted one. A runtime or hosted driver always has one ([model] context_bytes, else its default)

run budget.about: every ceiling the run enforces, beside rpc.events' max_iterations (#799): max_wall_clock_ms, the wall-clock ceiling in milliseconds, checked against elapsed_ms; max_tokens, the token ceiling under the budget's own name ([budget] max_tokens) and in tokens, checked against the turn's completion_tokens_used and so a ceiling on completion tokens only; context_bytes, the ceiling on one prompt in bytes ([model] context_bytes as the driver enforces it), against which older observations are elided (the compacted event). A run budget sent again after a set_budget raise (#807) carries each of these too; context_bytes is never raised

compacted.about: sent when a model request would have exceeded the run's context budget in bytes and older observations were elided to fit it: turn is the turn that request produced; turns 1 to elided_turns have their observations elided from it on, which held elided_bytes; request_bytes is the request's size after eliding and budget the budget in force. Sent again only when another turn is elided.

compacted on request.about: sent as the request after a client's compact is built, when it folded at least one turn; the compact's answer carries the same figures (responses.compact)

plan.about: the model's plan (ADR 0058 section 5, #810), sent after the turn of a plan call the gates let through, and only in a run whose repository enables the tool ([tools] enable = ["plan"]); a disabled or declined plan call sends none. turn is that turn's number. steps is the plan as kept, a JSON array in one string, since an event's fields are flat: each element {"text", "state"}, state one of todo, current and done, in the model's order. At most eight are kept, each text at most 200 characters: steps_cut is how many steps past the eighth were dropped and texts_cut how many kept texts were shortened, so a client can say the plan was cut. The text and the state are the model's words (rule 1): a client shows them as text, never interprets them (CLAUDE.md rule 10), and makes no count of done steps. A later plan event replaces the earlier one. A person's edit to the plan goes back as a steer; nothing edits this plan but the model's next plan call

paused.about: the run is held (ADR 0058 section 1, #806): sent once, when the loop reaches the hold a client's pause asked for, at the top of an iteration after the model request in flight and the tool call it chose have finished, and before the pause is answered. turn is the model call it holds before, numbered as the model call event numbers it. While held the run asks the model nothing; steer and follow_up are accepted and wait, so a steer sent now is in the first request after resumed; approve, abort and quit are read as always, and an abort ends the held run with its rollback and no resumed event. Held time is not charged to the wall clock (elapsed_ms)

resumed.about: the held run goes on (#806): sent by the loop as it leaves the hold, after a client's resume or when rpc's input ends, since nothing could resume it then. turn is the paused event's; paused_ms is how long it was held, in milliseconds by the monotonic clock, the time left out of elapsed_ms and so of the wall-clock budget

null_when.request_id: the prompt or follow_up whose run asks was sent with no id

approval_request.about: request_id is the id of the prompt or follow_up whose run asks the question

pause.about: takes no fields (ADR 0058 section 1, #806) and is answered once the loop holds, after the paused event: turn is the model call it holds before. Refused with no run in flight; already paused while a pause is held or still asked for; and, after the run's run_end, with the run ended before it reached the hold when the run ended first. A resume before the hold is reached withdraws the pause, which is then refused saying so. When rpc's input ends a pause still waiting is refused and a held run goes on.

resume.about: takes no fields and has no data (#806): answered at once, and the loop's resumed event says how long the run was held. Refused with no run in flight, and not paused when no pause is held or asked for. Before the hold is reached it withdraws the pause, and the run goes on without holding.

set_budget.about: {max_iterations?, max_wall_clock_ms?, max_tokens?}, at least one, raises the run in flight's ceilings under the names and units run budget sends them in (ADR 0058 section 2, #807), and is answered at once with every ceiling after the change. A raise is to the run's whole ceiling; a partitioned run would deal it through its shares, never grant it to each partition (CLAUDE.md rule 9). It takes effect at the loop's next budget check, at the top of its next iteration, after any pause and before the steering drain, where run budget is sent again; a tool call or check already under way finishes under the ceiling it started with. A raise that lifts every exhausted ceiling above the spend after the run's one extra turn was granted ends that escalation. A value equal to the ceiling in force changes nothing and sends no run budget, and so does a raise accepted during the run's last turn, which reaches no budget check. Refused whole, changing nothing: with no run in flight; before the loop's first budget check, and once the loop has returned; for a value below the ceiling in force, naming it; for a value that is not a whole number above 0, or for max_iterations one past 4294967295; for context_bytes, the driver's, fixed for the run; for any other field; and with no ceiling named. Recorded in no trail until #868.

withdraw.about: {id}, the command's own id as approve's is, names the steer or follow_up to take back by the id it was sent with (ADR 0058 section 3, #808); answered at once with that id and the message's type once it is withdrawn. The withdrawn message is never delivered: a steer is in no model request and its own steer response is answered success false, so a client reads two responses with this id, told apart by command; a follow_up's run never starts. It leaves get_state's pending and is not in abort's undelivered. The loop's drain and withdraw decide under one lock, so a steer is either withdrawn or delivered, never both. With several messages sent under one id, the first still waiting is taken. Refused, changing nothing: already delivered once a model request carries the steer or the follow_up's run has started; unknown id when no steer or follow_up waiting in the run in flight, or queued behind it, carries the id (the prompt's own id, and a message delivered in an earlier run of the chain, among them); no run in flight; and an id that is missing or not a non-empty string. Recorded in no trail until #868: a message withdrawn before the loop's drain reached it is in no steering record, and a steer or follow_up withdrawn after the drain set it aside (a follow_up, or a steer drained as the run ended) stays in that run's record as set aside.

read_file.about: {path} answers with one file's text for a whole-file view (ADR 0058 section 4, #809), read-only. path is repository-relative and is refused, by the rule it breaks, when it is absolute, holds a .. component or a control character (list_paths' prefix rule), when list_paths would not offer it (tracked, or untracked and not ignored, byte for byte as git spells it with /), when it resolves outside the root or into .git through a link (trellis_core::paths::resolve_repo_input), when it is not a file, and when the bytes read are not UTF-8. path is the path asked; bytes is the file's size on disk; text is at most 262144 bytes (256 KiB, a display limit), and a file past that is cut at the last whole character before it, with cut true. Bytes past the cap are not read, so they are not checked for UTF-8. text is repository text: a client shows it and never interprets it (CLAUDE.md rule 10), and nothing it answers enters a prompt.

null_when.configured: neither the repository's config nor the user's sets [model] spec
null_when.probed[].error: the runtime answered; local then holds the specs it listed that first_run would offer
null_when.providers[].key_variable: the provider's protocol is not one trellis knows

list_models.about: local holds the specs first_run would offer: vllm:http://<address>#<model> for a runtime, and provider:colibri#<model> for a /v1/models list owned by colibri (#625), which set_model {save: true} saves with the [[providers]] colibri entry it resolves through, key_variable COLI_API_KEY, in the user config only; probed names every address tried, in first_run's order (Ollama, llama.cpp, vLLM on their default ports); providers are the user config's [[providers]], by name and the variable a key would be read from, never its value (#564)

null_when.saved_to: save was not asked for, or the model is the configured one confirmed

set_model.about: {model, save?} names this session's model, and with save true writes it to the user's config file, never .trellis/config.toml; {configured: true} confirms the configured spec. Until one has succeeded, prompt is refused with an error that starts "choose a model first" (#564)

get_codebase.index_saved: true when the worktree's index was saved to .trellis/index.bin (#654, the owner's decision of 2026-10-12), through the writer trellis index uses; index_bytes is then the bytes written. false with index_not_saved (why) when a ref was asked for, since a commit's graph is never saved as the worktree's cache, or when the write failed; a failed save never fails the answer.

null_when.commit: no ref was asked for, and the repository has no commit yet or git could not read HEAD; the worktree's graph is answered either way

get_codebase.head_error: git's message, trimmed, when no ref was asked for and git failed reading HEAD (a hand-made .git git refuses, say); absent when the repository simply has no commit. commit and date never fail the answer.
get_codebase.about: {limit?, edges?, ref?} (the desktop's Atlas, owner request of 2026-10-11). edges "all" lists every module edge, so each calls_not_drawn is 0; absent, at most ten per module are listed, as before. ref answers the graph of that commit's tree: ref as asked, commit its full id with any tag peeled, date its committer date in strict ISO 8601 with the commit's own offset. Without ref, commit and date are HEAD's, and the graph is the worktree's, which may have moved past HEAD. A ref that is not a non-empty string, holds a control character, starts with - or names no commit is refused by name.
get_codebase.path: the module's file, relative to the root and /-separated
get_codebase.refused_when: the root has no .git entry (a directory, or the file a worktree or submodule has): success is false, the error names the command, the root and the rule, and nothing under the root is read

get_radius.about: reach and doubt count different populations and are never divided (ADR 0014). reached (the symbols the radius reached, in the index's order) and sites (the call sites it walked, certain ones first, each kind nearest first) were added for the desktop's Atlas (owner request of 2026-10-11); each holds at most 2000, the rest counted in reached_not_listed and sites_not_listed, while reach keeps the whole counts. line is 1-based. refused_when as get_codebase.

get_symbols.about: {module?} (the desktop's Atlas, owner request of 2026-10-11): every definition the index holds, or one module's, in the index's order. name is the bare name; line and end_line are 1-based, from the index's byte span. calls_in counts call sites bound to it by a Resolved edge, calls_in_ambiguous call sites whose candidates include it, calls_out call sites in its own body bound by a Resolved edge: three counts, none a part or a share of another. modules_indexed is the whole index's. A module the index holds no file for is refused by name. refused_when as get_codebase.

null_when.head: the repository has no commit yet; churn, commits and tags are then empty
null_when.churn[].commits: no tag is listed (tags 0 was asked for, or HEAD's history holds none), so there is nothing to count from

get_history.about: {commits?, tags?} (default 20 and 12, each held to 200; the desktop's Atlas, owner request of 2026-10-11), all from git. windows_days is [30, 90, 365]: d30, d90 and d365 count the first-parent commits that changed the path in the run from HEAD back to the first commit dated before the window opens, measured from HEAD's committer date, not the clock. churn[].commits counts those after the oldest tag listed. A path is a row when either range changed it; last_commit and last_date name the newest such commit. commits are the newest on HEAD's first-parent line with the paths each changed against its first parent; tags the newest HEAD can reach, peeled and dated by their commits, newest first. Dates are strict ISO 8601 with the commit's own offset. subject is text a commit's author wrote. refused_when as get_codebase.

null_when.tasks[].assignee: the task names no agent profile
null_when.tasks[].waiting: the task is not pending, or nothing holds it back

empty_when.tasks[].blockers: the task waits on no other task

get_state.pending_about: each steer and follow_up sent and not yet delivered, oldest first: follow_ups queued behind the run in flight, then what was sent to that run (#801). A steer leaves it as the loop puts it in the model request that carries it, marked before its steer delivered event is written (#808), so a get_state read after that event never lists it; a follow_up leaves it when its own run starts. A steer still waiting when its run ends leaves it then, answered as not delivered. A withdrawn steer or follow_up leaves it when withdraw is answered (#808). message is the text as it was sent.
get_state.last_run: the last run's run_end framing fields, without type

null_when.run_request_id: no run is in flight, or the one in flight was started by a command sent with no id
null_when.model: neither set_model nor the configuration's [model] spec names one
null_when.last_run: no run of this rpc process has ended
null_when.tier: no run of this rpc process has decided its tier yet, or the last run stopped before deciding one; never guessed from the spec
null_when.pending[].id: the steer or follow_up was sent with no id

empty_when.pending: no run is in flight, or nothing sent to it is still waiting

tier_label.shape: <head>, or <head><detail_separator><detail>. A digit head is the adapter tier; unknown means nothing has established one; scripted means no model is called. <detail> is prose for a person (e.g. "native tool calls", "no schema", "unavailable: colibri olmoe refuses tools"), not a further format. A label never begins with the word tier: a status bar writes `tier ` before it.

steer.about: answered once a model request carries the steer: after_step is the step it followed, so the request after that step was the first to carry it. Refused, success false, when the run ends before another request, or when a withdraw takes it back first (#808).

null_when.undelivered[].id: the steer or follow_up was sent with no id

empty_when.undelivered: every steer reached a request and no follow_up was waiting, or a pending classify was dropped

abort.about: answered once the run has ended and rolled back: everything sent on the steering channel and never delivered, in the order received. A follow_up waiting behind the run is never run after an abort, so it is here.

approve.about: approved is the answer the approve gave, as true or false; an approve for a question trellis no longer holds is refused

compact.about: answered once the run's next model request has been built: turn is the turn that request produced; turns_folded the turns this compact elided, 0 when nothing was left to fold; turns 1 to elided_turns have their observations elided, which held elided_bytes; bytes_before and bytes_after are the request's size either side. Refused when the run ends before another request.

empty_when.prompts: the repository and its installed packages hold no prompt template

get_commands.about: prompts are the repository's templates (.trellis/prompts/<name>.md) and its installed packages', each sent as a prompt's prompt by name; description is the template's frontmatter description or its first line

null_when.models[].prompt_tokens: a run of that model did not report its prompt tokens
null_when.models[].completion_tokens: a run of that model did not report its completion tokens

empty_when.models: no run of this rpc process has written a trail that read back

get_session_stats.about: per model, over the trails of this process's runs (#313): two figures, never summed. runs_not_counted counts the runs whose trail did not read back, so the rows are not taken for the whole session.

null_when.configured.repository: the repository's config sets no [model] spec, or does not read
null_when.configured.user: the user's config sets no [model] spec
null_when.configured.session: no set_model has named this session's model

get_available_models.about: catalog is the weights trellis model pull fetches, download_gib rounded to a tenth; a catalogue name is not a spec. configured is each source's [model] spec; the repository's wins over the user's (ADR 0025 section 7).

null_when.text: no run of this rpc process has ended on done

get_last_assistant_text.about: the summary of the last run that ended on done: model output, a JSON string, read as nothing else (ADR 0007)

empty_when.hits: nothing in the vault matches the query

vault_search.about: what trellis vault search prints, in its order; mode says which of the index's reductions the search ran under. Strings are as the notes store them.

null_when.depth: the note is under a parent that does not resolve, or on a cycle
null_when.unresolved_parent: the note's parent resolves, or it names none

vault_graph.about: what trellis vault graph prints about one note: lineage and issues are lists of text; weight counts the links between the two notes. Strings are as the notes store them.

vault_check.about: what trellis vault check prints, never --fix's path: nothing is written. gate is the run gate's vault validation, not a Verdict (ADR 0004): whether a run would accept the vault, and nothing about code.

optional.trail.ended_at: on every trail written since #622; absent on one written before it
optional.trail.factual.steering: when a steer or follow_up was sent during the run (ADR 0034); absent when none was, and on an interrupted run, whose turns and steering are dropped with its loop

null_when.trail.factual.context: no turn of the run carried a prompt size: a scripted model, or an interrupted run, whose turns are dropped with its loop

not_every_client.about: listed for the summary level (story #790), which will read them, and kept out of always and optional above, every path of which the desktop's trails test requires its rows to carry; they move up once a client reads them. The fields inside radius, context, actions and steering are listed when a client reads them. trail is the run's trail as written, read back as untrusted data (ADR 0007).

overview.about: `trellis [--root <repo>] --json overview` prints one object (ADR 0050 section 3, ADR 0025 section 4, both amended 2026-10-07; #558), held by client_contract_overview_lists_what_the_overview_object_carries in tests/cli.rs. Outside a repository, or with a root that has no .git entry, it carries only the keys under outside_a_repository. A last_run, in recent or at the top, is null when there is no trail, {"error": <why>} when the newest trail will not parse, and otherwise the fields below. codebase is null when the cache is missing or stale, codebase_reason saying which (null when current). pr_ci.available false carries reason in place of pull_requests and runs. Strings from trails, the queue and gh are data written by others.

optional.recent_error: when the recent list cannot be read; recent is then empty
optional.last_run.error: in place of the other last_run fields, when the newest trail will not parse
optional.board.tasks_error: when the queue cannot be read; tasks is then null
